ranking.why: The only suspect whose cost scales with the per-rank shard and was never judged at TP3 (candidate-51's own mark: 'TP3's grid-4 case ... recorded ... but not judged'). Its single-thread issuer walks each window in 64 KiB chunks with a 200 ns %globaltimer pause between chunks, so a window's side-stream time is at least (chunks-2) x 200 ns regardless of how fast DRAM could fill it. TP3's windows are all at their budget caps (WO 20.0, FFN 16.0, NEXT 20.0 MB = 56.0 MB a layer, about 857 chunks) against TP4's 18.9/14.8/14.8 MB (48.5 MB, about 741 chunks): +16% bytes and pace floor, about 170 vs 148 us a layer. Windows queue on one side stream (a window issued while the previous one still fills starts when it ends), and the side stream rejoins the main stream only once, at model end (l2_prefetch.join in DeepseekV41Model.forward), so any lag accumulated over 40 layers lands on forward_ms, and a late fill also stops being an L2 hit and competes with the consumer's own DRAM read. That fits a fixed cost at 1 request that longer layers (more rows) absorb, and the exact mirror of the TP4 gain the same patch brought. Not yet measured: the sp8 A/B (c54 vs no961) decides it.
ranking.evidence: raw/boot-logs/ (plan sizes at TP3 and TP4), vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/l2_prefetch.py L2Prefetcher.issue/join, vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/l2_prefetch.py

But on the target side it only compacts embed_tokens into a new carve-out buffer (the head keeps its buffer and screening table); its other moves (markov_w1, 960 MiB of draft-expert slabs) are drafter-side, and the drafter got faster at 4-8 requests, as its own mark says. No mechanism for +1 ms of target forward is known.

Moves FULL-step attention/CED metadata prep into the captured target graph, so its device work now sits inside the forward_ms window (its own mark: 33-42 us device, less than before). Kernel-level packed-BF16 GEMM and vocab-exception changes; its rework timed TP3 and TP4 cells (decode M up to 128) and found no slower cell.
One more BF16 rounding in moe_swiglu_cast; its own mark timed TP3's inter=768 and found it not worse; a per-element cost would grow with rows, not shrink.

cause.leading_hypothesis: #961's paced single-issuer L2 prefetch: at TP3 the capped 20/16/20 MB windows take longer to issue than TP4's, the one prefetch side stream falls behind the main stream at small batches, and the model-end join waits for it.
cause.how_to_confirm_on_sp8: W/tools/queue.sh: c54 vs no961 (and noAll, no998, no960, no963-no1030) ABBA, forward_ms per cell. Then the variants in commands.txt section 5: prefetch off in both arms (the delta should vanish), TP4-sized budgets on c54 (VLLM_DS41_L2_PREFETCH_WO_MB=18.9, FFN 14.8, NEXT 14.8: should recover most of it if the window bytes are the cause), all-reduce stand-in 0 vs 30 us, and an Nsight Systems node trace of 1x3 in both arms showing whether the side stream ends after the main stream's last kernel.

if_961: First, recipe-only, measurable at once: cap TP3's windows at the bytes TP4 fills, through the existing per-window budgets in tp3-triangle's (so tp3-switched's and tp3-triangle-4k's) environment: VLLM_DS41_L2_PREFETCH_WO_MB / _FFN_MB / _NEXT_MB. It keeps #961's TP4 gain and changes no code.

Otherwise a narrow code follow-up to #961: make the pace follow the window, not a fixed 200 ns (e.g., a per-plan pace from its bytes, or a pace and issuer count from the environment, set per shape), so a TP3 window ends inside its window; or go back to the grid-2 4 KiB kernel at TP3 only.
Judge it by the same TP3 grid cells (sp8 harness, then the 6-boot spec) and keep TP4's cells where candidate-54 has them.
